description: The user in the conversation types instructions that override the developer's intent.
Instructions hidden in content the model reads on someone's behalf: web pages, email, documents, tool results, memory. The victim never sees them.
An attack on the model's safety training. Different from injection, which attacks the application by making the model follow someone else's instructions.
An attacker who iterates against your specific defense (search, optimization, human creativity) instead of replaying a fixed list. Most published defenses fall to it.
Delimiting, marking or encoding untrusted text so the model can tell it apart from instructions. Lowers attack success; does not eliminate it.
A privileged model with tools sees only trusted input; a quarantined model without tools reads untrusted text, and its results travel as references.
Google DeepMind's 2025 design: a program extracted from the trusted query, a quarantined model for untrusted data, and capabilities checked at every tool call.
Meta, October 2025: per session, at most two of untrusted input, sensitive data or systems, and state changes or external communication; all three need a human.
